title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Generalization to General Compact Metric Spaces

problemStatement.formal: \text{For compact metrizable } X \text{ with } \dim(X) \leq n, \text{ every } f \in C(X, \mathbb{R}) \text{ has } f(x) = \sum_{q=0}^{2n} \Phi_q(g_q(x)) \text{ with continuous } \Phi_q, g_q
problemStatement.plain: The Kolmogorov-Arnold theorem generalizes from [0,1]^n to arbitrary compact metric spaces: covering dimension n implies every continuous function decomposes into 2n+1 compositions of univariate functions. Sternfeld showed this is both necessary and sufficient.

Generalizes the classical KA theorem to the natural level of generality
The 2n+1 bound is sharp — cannot be improved even in the general setting

# Knowledge Base: hilbert-13-oq-04

Insights accumulated during research on this problem.

---

## Problem Understanding

The Kolmogorov-Arnold theorem generalizes from [0,1]^n to compact metrizable spaces. The key insight is that covering dimension is the precise invariant controlling superposition representations. Sternfeld (1985) proved the complete characterization: superposition with 2n+1 maps iff dim <= n.

---

## Insights

- Covering dimension is not in Mathlib — this is genuinely new infrastructure
- The Sternfeld characterization is an iff, giving both necessity and sufficiency
- Ostrand's separating maps (1965) bridge dimension theory and representation theory
- The 2n+1 bound is sharp even in the general setting
